The search results include only one specific product, so I can't say it's the best on the market. The **Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100 W)** is a good airline-legal pick, especially if you want to charge a laptop as well as a phone.

**Why it works for flying**
- **Under the limit:** It's about 74 Wh, below the 100 Wh per-battery cap the FAA sets for power banks in carry-on bags. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries))
- **Output:** It has 100 W USB-C output, 2× USB-C and 2× USB-A ports, and pass-through charging. It's flat (134 × 134 × 18 mm, about 451 g) and comes with a 100 W cable.
- **Price and warranty:** $89.99 at Baseus's US store (checked 2026-10-21), with a 24-month warranty. ([Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah))
- **Buy:** [Baseus Blade H1 at Baseus's official US store](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no extra cost to you. The listing says no discount codes work on this product.

**Airline rules to know, whichever bank you buy**
- **Carry-on only:** Power banks can't go in checked bags. If your carry-on is gate-checked, take the bank out first and keep it with you. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **Terminal protection:** Protect the terminals from short circuit, for example with the original packaging, a pouch, or tape. ([IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/))
- **Airline limits:** Airlines can be stricter than the FAA. Southwest, for example, has allowed only one power bank per customer since April 20, 2026. It must be 100 Wh or less and kept out of the overhead bin. You can't charge it from in-seat power, and it must be visible while in use. ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters))

If you only need to top up a phone, a smaller and cheaper bank would probably do, but the results didn't cover any. Tell me your airline and what you'll be charging, and I can narrow it down.
